findings.title: Substring matching enables upsampling for non-error queries
findings.body: This check matches `event.type:error` anywhere in the query, including negated filters such as `!event.type:error` and mixed queries such as `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. Those queries include non-error events, but the rewritten aggregation sums `sample_weight`, which is not defined for transactions. The result can undercount events or make the query fail; determine that the query positively restricts results to errors instead of searching for a substring.

findings.title: Error-split dashboard queries use the original dataset for eligibility
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives a `scoped_dataset`, but this check passes the outer `dataset` selected for the request. For a metrics-enhanced dashboard widget split into `ERROR_EVENTS`, the caller executes the error query against `discover` while the outer dataset remains a metrics dataset, so `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` rejects it and the split error count stays unupsampled. The eligibility check needs to reflect the dataset and query actually being executed.

findings.title: The errors dataset uses an aggregation registered only for discover
findings.body: This branch enables transformation for the `errors` dataset, causing `count()` to become `upsampled_count()`. The new function is registered only in `DiscoverDataset.function_converter` in `src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py`; the errors dataset cannot resolve that function, so allowlisted requests using that dataset fail when the rewritten query is built. Register the function for the errors query path too, or avoid rewriting that dataset.
